item.content:encoded:
If you say “I eat,” “I ate,” “I am eating,” and “I will eat,” the main verb changes the way your listener understands time, action, and context.

That is the basic idea behind tense.

Tense is one of the most important parts of English grammar because it helps us explain when something happens, whether an action is finished, whether it is continuing, and how one event relates to another.

For beginners, however, English tenses can feel unnecessarily complicated. You may hear about 12 tenses, memorize formulas, and still hesitate when choosing between sentences such as:

  • I went to school.
  • I was going to school.
  • I have gone to school.
  • I had gone to school.
  • I will go to school.

The good news is that you do not need to memorize dozens of rules without understanding them.

Once you understand the relationship between time and aspect, English tenses become much easier.

In this guide, we will explain what tense means, the commonly taught 12 English tenses, when to use each one, practical examples, common mistakes, and a simple method for learning them.

What Is Tense in English Grammar?

Tense is a grammatical form of a verb used to indicate the time of an action, event, or state.

Cambridge Dictionary defines tense as a form of a verb that shows the time at which an action happened. For example, “I sing” is present tense, while “I sang” is past tense.

Consider these sentences:

I study English.

I studied English yesterday.

I will study English tomorrow.

The verb forms help us understand the time being discussed.

  • study → present
  • studied → past
  • will study → future form

There is an important technical point here. In linguistic terms, English has only two grammatical tenses marked directly on the verb: present and past. English expresses future time through structures such as will, be going to, and present-tense forms used for future situations. The British Council and Cambridge Dictionary both explain this distinction.

However, English-learning textbooks commonly teach 12 tenses, combining tense with aspect and time. This traditional system is extremely useful for beginners, so we will use it throughout this guide.

Why Is Tense Important in English?

Imagine someone tells you:

“I eat dinner.”

You understand that eating is presented as a present or habitual action.

Now compare:

“I ate dinner.”

The action happened in the past.

And:

“I am eating dinner.”

The action is currently in progress.

The difference is small in vocabulary but significant in meaning.

Tense helps you communicate:

  • when an action happens
  • whether an action is finished
  • whether an action is continuing
  • whether an action happened before another event
  • whether something is planned or expected
  • how long an action has continued

This matters in everyday conversation, academic writing, professional communication, storytelling, examinations, and English proficiency tests.

A sentence with the wrong tense can change the meaning completely.

Example

I live in Dhaka.

This normally describes your current situation.

I lived in Dhaka.

This normally suggests that you lived there in the past and may not live there now.

The tense gives the listener important information without requiring additional explanation.

The Basic Idea Behind English Tenses

Before learning the 12 commonly taught tenses, understand two concepts:

  1. Time
  2. Aspect

1. Time

English grammar commonly discusses three time references:

  • Present
  • Past
  • Future

2. Aspect

Aspect describes how an action relates to time.

The four commonly taught aspects are:

  • Simple: an action or state viewed generally
  • Continuous: an action in progress
  • Perfect: an action viewed in relation to another time
  • Perfect continuous: emphasizes duration or ongoing activity in relation to another time

When these concepts are combined, we get the familiar 12-tense framework.

Time Simple Continuous Perfect Perfect Continuous
Present Present Simple Present Continuous Present Perfect Present Perfect Continuous
Past Past Simple Past Continuous Past Perfect Past Perfect Continuous
Future Future Simple Future Continuous Future Perfect Future Perfect Continuous

Do not try to memorize this table immediately.

Instead, understand what each pattern means.

The 12 English Tenses Explained

1. Present Simple Tense

The present simple is used for things that happen regularly, facts, general truths, routines, and permanent or relatively stable situations.

Structure

Subject + base verb

For third-person singular subjects such as he, she, and it, the verb usually takes -s or -es.

Examples

  • I work every day.
  • You study English.
  • They play football.
  • She works in a bank.
  • He watches television at night.
  • The sun rises in the east.

When to use the present simple

Use it for:

Habits

I drink tea every morning.

Regular activities

She goes to university by bus.

Facts

Water boils at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure.

General truths

Practice improves your skills.

Permanent or long-term situations

He lives in Bangladesh.

Common time expressions

  • always
  • usually
  • often
  • sometimes
  • rarely
  • never
  • every day
  • every week

Common mistake

Incorrect:

She work in a hospital.

Correct:

She works in a hospital.

Remember the third-person singular -s/-es in the present simple. Cambridge's grammar guidance notes that regular verbs use the -s form with third-person singular subjects.

2. Present Continuous Tense

The present continuous describes an action that is happening now or around the present period.

Structure

Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing

Examples

  • I am studying English.
  • She is watching a movie.
  • They are playing football.
  • We are learning grammar.
  • He is working on a project.

When to use it

Use the present continuous for an action happening right now:

I am writing an article.

You can also use it for a temporary situation:

I am staying with my friend this week.

It can also describe a developing situation:

Technology is changing rapidly.

Present Simple vs Present Continuous

Compare:

I work from home.

This suggests a regular or normal situation.

I am working from home today.

This emphasizes the situation happening today.

This distinction is extremely important for beginners.

3. Present Perfect Tense

The present perfect connects a past action or situation with the present.

Structure

Subject + have/has + past participle

Examples

  • I have finished my homework.
  • She has visited London.
  • They have completed the project.
  • He has lost his phone.
  • We have studied this topic before.

The British Council explains that the present perfect is used for past actions or states that remain connected to the present.

When to use it

Use the present perfect when:

The exact past time is not important

I have seen that movie.

The result matters now

I have lost my keys.

The important meaning is that the keys are still missing.

Talking about experience

I have visited several countries.

Talking about an unfinished period

I have read three chapters this week.

Present Perfect vs Past Simple

This is one of the most common beginner problems.

I visited London in 2024.

The time is finished and specifically identified.

I have visited London.

The experience is important, but no finished past time is specified.

4. Present Perfect Continuous Tense

The present perfect continuous emphasizes an activity that started in the past and has continued up to the present, or has recently stopped with a visible result.

Structure

Subject + have/has + been + verb-ing

Examples

I have been studying for three hours.

She has been working here since January.

They have been waiting for the bus.

For duration

Use for with a period of time:

I have been learning English for two years.

Use since with a starting point:

I have been learning English since 2024.

Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous

Compare:

I have written five pages.

The focus is on the completed result.

I have been writing for three hours.

The focus is on the activity and its duration.

5. Past Simple Tense

The past simple describes an action or situation that happened and finished in the past.

Structure

For regular verbs:

Subject + verb-ed

For irregular verbs, use the appropriate past form.

Examples

  • I watched a movie yesterday.
  • She visited her grandmother.
  • They played football last Friday.
  • He went to school.
  • We studied English last night.

Common time expressions

  • yesterday
  • last week
  • last year
  • two days ago
  • in 2020
  • when I was young

Regular and irregular verbs

Regular:

work → worked

play → played

watch → watched

Irregular:

go → went

eat → ate

see → saw

write → wrote

English verbs have several forms, including the base form, past form, past participle, -ing form, and third-person singular present form.

6. Past Continuous Tense

The past continuous describes an action that was in progress at a particular moment in the past.

Structure

Subject + was/were + verb-ing

Examples

I was studying at 9 p.m.

She was cooking dinner.

They were playing football when it started raining.

Past Continuous + Past Simple

These two tenses often work together.

I was walking home when I saw my friend.

Here:

  • was walking = ongoing background action
  • saw = shorter event that happened during it

Another example:

She was sleeping when the phone rang.

This pattern is especially useful when telling stories.

7. Past Perfect Tense

The past perfect describes an action that happened before another past action.

Structure

Subject + had + past participle

Example

I had finished my homework before my friend arrived.

There are two past events:

  1. I finished my homework.
  2. My friend arrived.

The homework was finished first.

The past perfect makes that sequence clear.

More examples

She had already left when I arrived.

They had eaten dinner before the movie started.

He had never visited Dhaka before that trip.

A useful rule

When discussing two past events, ask:

Which happened first?

If you need to emphasize the earlier event, past perfect is often appropriate.

8. Past Perfect Continuous Tense

The past perfect continuous emphasizes an activity that continued for a period before another point in the past.

Structure

Subject + had been + verb-ing

Examples

I had been studying for three hours when my friend called.

She had been working there for five years before she moved abroad.

They had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.

The focus is on duration before a past event.

Compare:

I had studied for three hours.

This focuses more generally on the completed activity.

I had been studying for three hours.

This emphasizes the ongoing activity and its duration.

9. Future Simple Tense

The future simple, commonly taught using will, is used for predictions, decisions made at the moment of speaking, promises, offers, and other future situations.

Structure

Subject + will + base verb

Examples

I will call you tomorrow.

She will help you.

They will arrive soon.

I think it will rain.

I will finish the work tonight.

Instant decisions

“The phone is ringing.”

“I will answer it.”

The decision is made at the moment of speaking.

Predictions

I think Bangladesh will win.

Promises

I will help you with your homework.

10. Future Continuous Tense

The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a particular time in the future.

Structure

Subject + will be + verb-ing

Examples

I will be studying at 8 p.m.

She will be traveling tomorrow afternoon.

They will be working during the evening.

Imagine someone asks:

What will you be doing at 10 tomorrow morning?

You could answer:

I will be attending a class.

The tense emphasizes an activity that will be underway at that future moment.

11. Future Perfect Tense

The future perfect describes an action that will be completed before a particular future time.

Structure

Subject + will have + past participle

Examples

I will have finished the project by Friday.

She will have arrived by 8 p.m.

They will have completed the course by next month.

The key expression is often by + future time.

For example:

By next year, I will have completed my degree.

The sentence looks forward from now and imagines the completed result at a future point.

12. Future Perfect Continuous Tense

The future perfect continuous emphasizes how long an activity will have continued up to a particular future time.

Structure

Subject + will have been + verb-ing

Examples

By June, I will have been studying English for three years.

Next month, she will have been working here for five years.

By 10 p.m., they will have been traveling for twelve hours.

This tense is less common in everyday conversation than the simpler forms, but it is useful when you need to emphasize duration leading up to a future point.

English Tenses at a Glance

Here is a simple reference table:

Tense Basic Structure Example
Present Simple subject + verb I study English.
Present Continuous am/is/are + verb-ing I am studying English.
Present Perfect have/has + past participle I have studied English.
Present Perfect Continuous have/has been + verb-ing I have been studying English.
Past Simple subject + past verb I studied English.
Past Continuous was/were + verb-ing I was studying English.
Past Perfect had + past participle I had studied English.
Past Perfect Continuous had been + verb-ing I had been studying English.
Future Simple will + verb I will study English.
Future Continuous will be + verb-ing I will be studying English.
Future Perfect will have + past participle I will have studied English.
Future Perfect Continuous will have been + verb-ing I will have been studying English.

How to Choose the Correct Tense

Instead of memorizing formulas first, ask yourself three questions.

Question 1: When is the action happening?

Is it:

  • Present?
  • Past?
  • Future?

For example:

I ___ football yesterday.

“Yesterday” tells you that the action happened in the past.

So a past form is needed:

I played football yesterday.

Question 2: Is the action complete or in progress?

Compare:

I studied at 8 p.m.

and:

I was studying at 8 p.m.

The first simply reports the activity.

The second emphasizes that the activity was in progress at that time.

Question 3: Is there a connection between two times?

Consider:

She left before I arrived.

You can make the sequence clearer with:

She had left before I arrived.

The past perfect identifies the earlier event.

This three-question method is much more useful than trying to remember twelve formulas independently.

Practical Example: Tenses in a Real-Life Story

Imagine you are telling a friend about your trip.

You might say:

I live in Dhaka, and I usually travel during holidays. Last year, I visited Cox's Bazar. While I was walking along the beach, I met an old friend. Before that trip, I had never visited the area. I have already planned my next trip, and next month I will be traveling to another city. By the end of the year, I will have visited several new places.

Notice how different tenses work together.

  • live → current situation
  • usually travel → habit
  • visited → completed past event
  • was walking → action in progress
  • met → event during that action
  • had never visited → experience before another past event
  • have already planned → past action connected to the present
  • will be traveling → future activity in progress
  • will have visited → completed future result

This is how native and proficient English speakers actually use tense: multiple forms work together to build a clear timeline.

Common Tense Mistakes Beginners Make

1. Forgetting the Third-Person -s

Incorrect:

He play football every day.

Correct:

He plays football every day.

2. Using Present Simple for an Action Happening Now

Incorrect:

I study now.

If you mean that you are currently in the middle of studying:

I am studying now.

However, “I study now” can be grammatical in a different context, such as describing a current routine or contrast.

3. Using Past Simple With an Unfinished Time

Incorrect in many contexts:

I went to the gym today.

This is not automatically wrong. If the day is still ongoing, “I have been to the gym today” may be more appropriate when emphasizing present relevance.

The important point is that tense depends on the speaker's intended meaning and whether the time period is considered finished.

4. Confusing “Since” and “For”

Use since for a starting point:

I have lived here since 2020.

Use for for a duration:

I have lived here for six years.

5. Confusing “Have” and “Had”

Compare:

I have finished my work.

The action is connected to the present.

I had finished my work before he arrived.

The action happened before another past event.

6. Using “Will” Everywhere for the Future

English does not express every future meaning with will.

For example:

I am meeting my friend tomorrow.

This present continuous form can describe a planned future arrangement.

You can also use:

I am going to study tonight.

The British Council and Cambridge both note that English uses several structures to express future time, including will, be going to, present continuous, and present simple in appropriate contexts.

Tense vs Time: An Important Difference

One of the most useful concepts for advanced beginners is that grammatical tense and real-world time are not always identical.

For example:

The train leaves at 8 tomorrow morning.

The verb leaves is grammatically present tense, but the event happens in the future.

Similarly:

If I see him tomorrow, I will tell him.

The verb see is present tense, even though the meeting is expected to happen in the future.

English uses present forms for certain future meanings.

Cambridge Dictionary specifically notes that present forms can refer to future events and that English does not have a separate future tense form in the same way that present and past forms are grammatically marked.

This is why simply translating every sentence from your native language into English can produce unnatural or incorrect tense choices.

Expert Tips for Learning English Tenses

1. Learn Meaning Before Formula

Do not begin with:

Subject + had + V3

Begin with:

“I use this when one past event happened before another past event.”

Then learn:

Subject + had + past participle.

Meaning gives the formula a purpose.

2. Learn Tenses in Groups

Do not attempt to memorize all 12 at once.

Start with:

Group 1: Basic

  • Present Simple
  • Past Simple
  • Future Simple

Group 2: Actions in Progress

  • Present Continuous
  • Past Continuous
  • Future Continuous

Group 3: Completed or Connected Actions

  • Present Perfect
  • Past Perfect
  • Future Perfect

Group 4: Duration

  • Present Perfect Continuous
  • Past Perfect Continuous
  • Future Perfect Continuous

This makes the system much easier to understand.

3. Use One Verb to Practice Everything

Take the verb study.

Write:

I study English.

I am studying English.

I have studied English.

I have been studying English.

Then move to the past:

I studied English.

I was studying English.

I had studied English.

I had been studying English.

Then the future:

I will study English.

I will be studying English.

I will have studied English.

I will have been studying English.

This technique helps you see the pattern rather than memorizing isolated examples.

4. Build a Timeline

When confused, draw a simple timeline.

For example:

Past → Earlier event → Later event → Present → Future

Then ask where each action belongs.

This is particularly useful for distinguishing:

  • past simple vs past perfect
  • past simple vs present perfect
  • present perfect vs present perfect continuous
  • future simple vs future perfect

5. Read Real English

Grammar exercises are useful, but real English shows you how tenses behave in context.

Read:

  • news articles
  • books
  • blogs
  • interviews
  • essays
  • transcripts
  • English-learning resources

Do not simply underline every tense.

Ask:

Why did the writer choose this tense here?

That question develops grammatical awareness.

A Simple Daily Practice Routine

You can improve your tense usage with 15–20 minutes of practice each day.

Step 1: Write about today

Use present forms.

I wake up at 7. I usually have breakfast at 8. I am studying English today.

Step 2: Write about yesterday

Use past forms.

Yesterday, I woke up at 7. I went to class. I was studying when my friend called.

Step 3: Write about your experience

Use present perfect.

I have visited several cities. I have learned many new things.

Step 4: Write about your plans

Use future forms.

I will visit another city next month. I am going to start a new course.

Step 5: Explain the tense choices

This final step is important.

Do not just write the sentences. Explain why you selected each tense.

That turns passive memorization into active grammar practice.

Frequently Asked Questions About Tense

How many tenses are there in English?

English-learning materials commonly teach 12 tenses: four present, four past, and four future forms.

Technically, however, linguists often distinguish grammatical tense from aspect. English has present and past tense forms, while future time is expressed through several constructions rather than a dedicated future verb inflection.

What is the easiest tense to learn first?

Start with the present simple, past simple, and future simple.

These give you the basic concept of present, past, and future time before you move to continuous and perfect forms.

What is the difference between tense and aspect?

Tense primarily relates to grammatical time, while aspect describes how an action is viewed in relation to time, such as whether it is ongoing or completed in relation to another point.

The traditional 12-tense system combines these concepts for teaching purposes.

Which tense is most commonly used in English?

There is no single tense that should be used for every situation. The present simple is extremely common because it is used for routines, facts, states, and general statements, but different contexts naturally require different forms.

Why is present perfect difficult for beginners?

Many learners struggle with present perfect because its meaning does not always map directly onto the tense system of their first language.

The key idea is to look for a connection between a past action and the present, rather than simply thinking “past.”

Can present tense talk about the future?

Yes.

For example:

The train leaves at 8 tomorrow.

The present simple can describe scheduled future events.

The present continuous can also describe arrangements:

I am meeting my friend tomorrow.

English uses several grammatical structures to refer to future time.

What is the difference between “I went” and “I have gone”?

I went uses the past simple and normally refers to a completed past event.

I have gone uses the present perfect and presents the action as connected to the present.

The surrounding context determines the exact interpretation.

Do I need to memorize all 12 tenses?

Not immediately.

A better approach is to learn the meaning and common uses of each tense, then practice them in real sentences.

Once the patterns become familiar, the formulas become much easier to remember.

Final Takeaways

Tense is not simply a collection of grammar formulas to memorize.

It is a system that helps you show when something happens and how an action relates to time.

For beginners, remember these core ideas:

  1. Present Simple → habits, facts, routines, states.
  2. Present Continuous → actions happening around now or temporary situations.
  3. Present Perfect → past actions connected to the present.
  4. Present Perfect Continuous → activity or duration continuing toward the present.
  5. Past Simple → completed past events.
  6. Past Continuous → actions in progress at a past time.
  7. Past Perfect → an earlier action before another past event.
  8. Past Perfect Continuous → duration leading up to a past event.
  9. Future Simple → future decisions, predictions, promises, and other future meanings.
  10. Future Continuous → an action that will be in progress at a future time.
  11. Future Perfect → something completed before a future point.
  12. Future Perfect Continuous → duration continuing up to a future point.

Most importantly, do not learn tense as a formula-only subject.

When you write or speak, first think about the timeline:

When did it happen? Is it happening now? Will it happen later? Is it finished? Is it continuing? Did it happen before something else?

Once you can answer those questions, choosing the correct tense becomes much more natural.

The goal is not to memorize twelve boxes on a grammar chart. The goal is to use verb forms accurately enough that your listener or reader immediately understands when an action happened, how it developed, and how it relates to everything else in your sentence.

Further reading

For reliable grammar references, see the British Council LearnEnglish grammar resources and Cambridge Dictionary's English Grammar Today.

item.title: How to Write an Application: Format and Examples
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Learn how to write applications with simple formats and examples for leave, testimonial, transcript, study tour, SSC, HSC, university, and jobs.
item.content:encoded:
Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons.

For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes.

The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation.

This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications.

What Is an Application?

An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority.

For example:

  • A student writes to the headmaster for leave.
  • A student writes to the principal for a testimonial.
  • A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript.
  • A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour.
  • A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position.

The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting.

Basic Application Writing Format

A formal application usually contains these parts:

  1. Date
  2. Name and designation of the recipient
  3. Institution or organisation
  4. Address
  5. Subject
  6. Salutation
  7. Main body
  8. Closing
  9. Name and identifying information of the applicant

A simple structure looks like this:

Date

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing.

Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation.

Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID]

The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer.

1. Application for Leave

A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution.

Example: Leave Application for Illness

15 January 2026

The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka

Subject: Application for leave of absence.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest.

For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17

What to include in a leave application

Make sure you mention:

  • The reason for your absence
  • The dates of your leave
  • Your class or department
  • Your roll or student ID
  • Any supporting document if the institution requires one

Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs.

2. Application for a Testimonial

A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution.

Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes.

Example: Testimonial Application

10 February 2026

The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka

Subject: Application for a testimonial.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356

Tip for students

If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details.

3. Application for an Academic Transcript

University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes.

The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents.

Example

22 March 2026

The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000

Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require an official academic transcript for my application for higher studies abroad.

I have completed the required payment and attached the necessary documents with this application.

I therefore request you to kindly issue two copies of my official academic transcript.

Yours faithfully, Mohammad Tanvir Ahmed Registration No. 2021-715-001 Session: 2020–2021 Department of CSE

Important

Before submitting a university application, check your university's current instructions. Do not assume that every university uses the same process.

4. Application for a Transfer Certificate

A transfer certificate application is generally written when a student needs official permission or documentation to leave one institution and continue studies elsewhere.

Example

20 April 2026

The Principal ABC College Dhaka

Subject: Application for a transfer certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class XII of your college. My family is moving to another city, and I need to continue my studies there.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a transfer certificate so that I can complete the necessary admission formalities at another institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Rahim Ahmed Class XII Roll No. 25 Science Group

5. Application for Permission to Join a Study Tour

Students may need permission from their school or college authority before joining an educational tour or study tour.

Example

5 May 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for permission to join a study tour.

Sir,

With due respect, we, the students of Class X, would like to arrange an educational study tour to the National Museum in Dhaka. Such a visit would give us an opportunity to learn more about the history and culture of Bangladesh outside the classroom.

We therefore request you to kindly grant us permission to arrange the study tour under the guidance of our teachers.

We shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, The students of Class X ABC High School Dhaka

Tip

For a group application, write on behalf of the students and clearly mention the proposed destination, purpose, and supervision arrangements when relevant.

6. Job Application Letter

A job application is different from a school application. Instead of asking a school authority for permission or a document, you are introducing yourself to an employer and explaining why you are suitable for a particular position.

A modern job application should be concise and specific.

Example

5 April 2026

The Head of Human Resources ABC Bank Limited Gulshan, Dhaka

Subject: Application for the position of Management Trainee Officer.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of Management Trainee Officer advertised on your company's website.

I recently completed my BBA in Finance from North South University with a CGPA of 3.78. During my undergraduate studies, I completed a three-month internship with a commercial bank, where I gained practical experience in credit analysis and customer service.

I believe my academic background, internship experience, and communication skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your organisation. My CV and relevant academic documents are attached for your consideration.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications in an interview.

Yours faithfully, Nusrat Jahan nusrat.jahan@example.com +880 1XXX-XXXXXX

Job application tip

Do not copy the same application for every job.

Mention the actual position, organisation, and skills that are relevant to the job. Your application should support your CV rather than repeat everything in it.

7. Application for a Character Certificate

A character certificate or similar official document may be requested for admission, employment, or other purposes.

The exact name and procedure can vary by institution.

Example

12 June 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for a character certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I was a student of your school and passed the SSC examination in 2026. I now require a character certificate for my further studies.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a character certificate mentioning my conduct and period of study at the institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sadia Islam SSC 2026 Roll No. 123456

How to Write an Application Step by Step

If you have never written a formal application before, follow these steps.

Step 1: Identify the person you are writing to

Find out who should receive the application.

For example:

  • The Headmaster
  • The Principal
  • The Head of the Department
  • The Controller of Examinations
  • The Human Resources Manager

Use the correct designation.

Step 2: Write a clear subject

The subject should tell the reader what you want.

Good examples:

  • Application for leave of absence
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for issuance of an academic transcript
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for permission to join a study tour

Do not write a long subject.

Step 3: Introduce yourself

Tell the reader who you are.

For example:

I am a student of Class X, Section A, of your school.

A university student could write:

I am a student of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.

Step 4: Explain the reason

Give the important facts related to your request.

For a leave application, mention the reason and dates.

For a testimonial, explain why you need it.

For a transcript, explain what you need and, if relevant, what the transcript is for.

Step 5: Make your request clearly

Do not make the reader guess what you want.

For example:

I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for three days.

Step 6: End politely

Use an appropriate formal closing.

For example:

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Then add your name and relevant identification details.

Common Mistakes in Application Writing

Students often make simple mistakes that can make an application look careless.

1. Forgetting the subject

The subject helps the reader understand the purpose of the application quickly.

2. Writing too much

A formal application should contain the information necessary to understand and process the request. Avoid unrelated stories.

3. Using informal language

Avoid expressions such as:

  • Hi Sir
  • What's up
  • I wanna request
  • Please help me out
  • Thanks a lot

Use polite and formal language instead.

4. Using unnecessary difficult words

You do not need complicated English to write a good application.

For example:

I would like to request you to kindly grant me leave.

is clear and sufficient.

A simple sentence is usually better than a long sentence filled with difficult words.

5. Forgetting personal details

For school and college applications, include the details needed to identify you, such as:

  • Name
  • Class
  • Section
  • Roll number
  • Registration number
  • Department
  • Student ID

Only include information that is relevant to the application.

6. Using the wrong closing

Choose the closing according to the situation and the style required by your institution.

For traditional school applications, “Yours obediently” is commonly used. For professional applications, “Yours faithfully” or “Yours sincerely” may be more appropriate depending on how you address the recipient.

Yours Obediently, Yours Faithfully, or Yours Sincerely?

These expressions are often confusing for students.

Yours obediently

This is commonly found in traditional school and college applications addressed to teachers or institutional authorities.

Yours faithfully

This is commonly used in formal correspondence when you do not address the recipient by name, especially in British-style business writing.

Example:

Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully,

Yours sincerely

This is commonly used when you address the recipient by name.

Example:

Dear Mr Karim, Yours sincerely,

However, institutions may have their own preferred format. If your school or university gives you a prescribed format, follow it.

Application Writing Format for SSC and HSC Students

For SSC and HSC students, application writing is also an important part of English writing practice.

Common topics include:

  • Application for leave
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for a seat in the school hostel
  • Application for permission to arrange a study tour
  • Application for setting up a canteen
  • Application for improving library facilities
  • Application for arranging a cultural programme

For examination practice, first understand the format. Then practise writing different applications instead of memorising one answer word for word.

A memorised application may not fit a new question exactly.

Application Writing vs. Formal Letter Writing

These two types of writing are related, but they have different purposes.

An application is usually a formal request made to an authority.

A formal letter can have a wider purpose, such as making a complaint, requesting information, giving notice, or communicating with an organisation.

For example:

Application: Application to the principal for leave.

Formal letter: Letter to the editor about traffic congestion in Dhaka.

Knowing the purpose helps you choose the right format.

Quick Application Writing Template

You can use this template when you need to write a new application.

[Date]

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am [your position/class/department].

[Explain the reason for your application and provide the important details.]

I therefore request you to kindly [clearly state what you want].

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/Student ID]

Use this as a framework, not as a paragraph to memorise. Change the details and sentences according to the situation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the format of an application in Bangladesh?

A formal application generally includes the date, recipient's designation and institution, subject, salutation, body, closing, and the applicant's identifying details. The exact format may vary depending on the institution.

How do I start an application?

Start by identifying the recipient and writing a clear subject. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself and explain the reason for writing.

How long should a formal application be?

For most school and college applications, one or two short paragraphs are enough. Include the necessary information without adding unrelated details.

Should I write an application by hand?

Follow the instructions of the institution or organisation. Some schools may prefer handwritten applications, while universities and employers may require typed or online submissions.

What paper size should I use?

If the institution has not specified a paper size, A4 is a practical choice for a typed formal document. However, always follow the instructions provided by the receiving institution.

Can I use the same application format for every topic?

You can use the same basic structure, but the content should change according to your purpose. A leave application, testimonial application, university transcript request, and job application should not contain the same body text.

Should I memorise application examples for exams?

It is better to understand the format and practise different topics. Memorising complete applications can make it difficult to answer questions that use a different situation.

Final Tips for Writing a Good Application

Before submitting your application, check these points:

  • Is the recipient correct?
  • Is the subject clear?
  • Did you explain the reason?
  • Did you make your request clear?
  • Did you include your class, roll, ID, or department where necessary?
  • Did you use polite and formal language?
  • Did you check spelling and grammar?
  • Did you follow any instructions given by the institution?
  • Did you remove unnecessary information?

A good application does not need complicated English. It needs a clear purpose, correct information, polite language, and a suitable format.

Once you understand the basic structure, you can write applications for school, college, university, and professional situations with much more confidence.

item.title: Top 10 Affordable Countries to Study Abroad for Bangladeshi Students
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Ranked list of the cheapest study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, covering tuition, living costs, scholarships, and work rights.
item.content:encoded:
Cost is usually the first real obstacle for Bangladeshi students who want to study abroad. Tuition is only part of it — visa fees, accommodation, food, transport, and health insurance can all add up quickly. The good news is that there are still plenty of countries where a serious student from Bangladesh can complete a quality degree without taking on crushing debt.

This guide ranks the ten most affordable study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, based on average annual tuition, living costs, scholarship availability, and post-study work rights. Costs are rough averages — your real budget will depend on the city, the university, and your lifestyle.

1. Germany

Public universities in Germany charge no tuition for bachelor's and most master's programmes, even for international students. You only pay a semester contribution of roughly €150–350. Annual living cost in cities like Leipzig, Dresden, or Aachen is around €9,000–11,000. A blocked account of €11,904 is required for the student visa. German universities offer hundreds of English-taught master's programmes in engineering, computer science, and business.

2. Norway

Public universities in Norway were free for everyone until 2023, and remain free for EU/EEA students. International students now pay tuition, but it is still moderate (NOK 80,000–250,000 a year depending on the programme). Living costs are higher than Germany, but part-time work rights are generous.

3. Malaysia

Malaysia is one of the most popular budget destinations for Bangladeshi students. Tuition at private universities typically runs USD 3,000–6,000 a year, and many UK/Australian universities have branch campuses (Monash, Nottingham, Reading) where you get the same degree at a fraction of the cost. Living expenses in Kuala Lumpur are around USD 4,000–5,000 a year.

4. Hungary

The Hungarian government's Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship is one of the most accessible fully funded options for Bangladeshi students. It covers tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and medical insurance. Even self-funded, Hungary is cheap: tuition is around €1,500–5,000 a year and living costs in Budapest are around €6,000–8,000.

5. Poland

Poland has become a quiet favourite. Tuition for English-taught programmes is around €2,000–4,000 a year, and cities like Kraków, Wrocław, and Warsaw offer good infrastructure and a large international student community. Living costs are similar to Hungary.

6. China

The Chinese government, provinces, and individual universities offer a huge number of scholarships (CSC, Confucius, Belt & Road) for Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is also cheap — RMB 18,000–35,000 a year. Living costs depend heavily on the city; tier-2 cities like Hefei or Wuhan are very affordable.

7. Russia

Russia offers the Open Doors and government scholarships, plus low-cost self-funded study (USD 2,500–6,000 a year). Medical universities in Russia are particularly popular for Bangladeshi students who couldn't get into BMDC-approved colleges at home, though you need to check the latest BMDC recognition list before committing.

8. Turkey

The Türkiye Bursları scholarship is fully funded and competitive. Self-funded tuition at Turkish state universities is around USD 500–1,500 a year. Istanbul and Ankara have lower living costs than most European cities.

9. India

India is geographically close, culturally familiar, and degrees from top Indian universities (IITs, IIMs, Delhi University, JNU) are well respected. The ICCR scholarship is offered specifically to Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is moderate, and living costs are the lowest on this list.

10. Czech Republic

Czech public universities are free if you study in Czech. English-taught programmes cost around €4,000–8,000 a year. Prague offers excellent quality of life and Czech degrees are recognised across the EU.

How to choose between them

Don't pick a country based only on cost. Consider:

  • Language of instruction — English-taught programmes are easier short-term, but learning the local language unlocks part-time jobs and post-study work.
  • Post-study work rights — Germany gives 18 months, Malaysia 12, Hungary 9. China and Russia are stricter.
  • Field of study — engineering and IT are well represented everywhere; arts and humanities are stronger in Western Europe.
  • IELTS requirement — most of these countries accept IELTS 6.0–6.5. Check your target university's exact requirement and use our IELTS Band Score Calculator to plan your prep.

FAQ

Which is the cheapest country to study abroad for Bangladeshi students?
Germany is the cheapest overall because public-university tuition is free. Hungary, Poland, and Malaysia are close behind if you include scholarships.

Can I work part-time while studying in these countries?
Yes — most of them allow 20 hours per week during term and full-time during holidays. Earnings depend heavily on the local minimum wage.

Do I need IELTS for all of them?
Almost always. A few universities accept MOI (Medium of Instruction) certificates from Bangladeshi institutions, but IELTS 6.0–6.5 is the safest baseline.

item.title: Study Tour Application: Format, Tips, and 5 Examples for Students
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Learn how to write a study tour application with the correct format. Includes 5 examples for school and college students plus simple writing tips.
item.content:encoded:
A study tour is an exciting part of student life. It allows students to visit historical places, industries, museums, universities, and different cities. Through these trips, students learn outside the classroom and gain real world knowledge.

However, before joining a tour, students usually need to submit a study tour application to their teacher, principal, or department head. This application asks for permission to participate in the tour.

In this guide, you will learn what a study tour application is, why schools require it, the proper format, useful writing tips, and several examples you can use as templates.

What Is a Study Tour Application?

A study tour application is a formal letter written by a student requesting permission to join an educational trip organized by a school, college, or university.

The application usually includes:

  • Student information
  • Purpose of the tour
  • Destination
  • Duration of the tour
  • A polite request for permission

Educational tours may include visits to museums, cultural places, industries, or universities. For example, students often visit famous educational locations such as the National Museum of Bangladesh or historical places like the Lalbagh Fort to learn about culture and history.

Because these tours involve travel and responsibility, institutions require formal permission requests.

Why Schools Require a Study Tour Application

Schools and colleges request applications for several important reasons.

1. Official Permission

The application allows teachers or principals to officially approve your participation in the tour.

2. Student Records

Institutions maintain records of students who are attending the trip.

3. Safety and Responsibility

If something unexpected happens during the tour, the school has documentation that the student received official permission.

4. Organization

Applications help schools manage the number of participants and make better arrangements for transportation and accommodation.

Format of a Study Tour Application

Writing a proper application is simple when you follow the correct structure.

1. Receiver Information

Start by addressing the person responsible for approving the tour.

Example:

To The Principal / Head Teacher School or College Name

2. Subject Line

Clearly mention the purpose of the letter.

Example:

Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour

3. Salutation

Use a polite greeting.

Example:

Respected Sir/Madam,

4. Body Paragraph

Explain your request clearly.

Include:

  • Tour destination
  • Tour date
  • Educational purpose

5. Closing

End with a polite request and gratitude.

Example:

I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

6. Signature

Finish with your details.

Example:

  • Your name
  • Class or department
  • Roll number
  • Date

Example 1: Study Tour Application for School Students

To The Principal ABC High School

Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour

Respected Sir,

I respectfully state that our school is organizing a study tour to the National Museum next week. The tour will help students learn more about the history and culture of our country.

I am very interested in joining this educational trip with my classmates. It will provide valuable learning experience outside the classroom.

Therefore, I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

Thank you for your consideration.

Yours obediently Raihan Class: 9 Roll: 12 Date: 16 March 2026

Example 2: Study Tour Application for College Students

To The Principal XYZ College

Subject: Application for permission to go on a study tour

Respected Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that our department has arranged a study tour to a historical site next month. The purpose of this tour is to help students gain practical knowledge related to our academic subjects.

I would like to join this tour along with my classmates. I believe the trip will enhance our understanding and provide valuable educational exposure.

Therefore, I kindly request you to allow me to participate in the study tour.

Yours faithfully Raihan Ahmed Department: History Roll: 24 Date: 16 March 2026

Example 3: Short Study Tour Application

To The Head Teacher ABC School

Subject: Permission for study tour

Respected Sir,

Our school is planning a study tour next week. I would like to participate in this educational trip with my classmates.

I kindly request you to grant me permission to join the study tour.

Thank you.

Yours obediently Raihan Class 10 Roll 5

Example 4: Application from Parents

Sometimes schools require permission from parents.

To The Principal ABC High School

Subject: Permission for my son to join the study tour

Respected Sir,

I am the father of Raihan, a student of class nine in your school. I have learned that the school is organizing a study tour next week.

I am happy to allow my son to participate in this educational trip. I believe it will be a great learning opportunity for him.

Thank you for organizing such activities for students.

Sincerely Mr. Karim Parent of Raihan

Example 5: Application for University Study Tour

To The Head of Department Department of Geography XYZ University

Subject: Request for permission to participate in study tour

Respected Sir,

Our department is arranging a study tour as part of the academic program. I am very interested in joining the trip because it will help me understand practical aspects of our course.

I believe the tour will improve our knowledge and provide valuable field experience.

Therefore, I request you to kindly grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

Yours sincerely Raihan Ahmed Department of Geography Student ID: 20345

Tips for Writing a Good Study Tour Application

Follow these tips to write a strong application.

Keep the Language Simple

Use clear and easy sentences so the reader quickly understands your request.

Be Polite

Always maintain a respectful tone when addressing teachers or principals.

Stay Short and Clear

An application should be brief. Avoid unnecessary details.

Include Important Information

Mention:

  • destination
  • purpose
  • date (if known)

Check Grammar

Before submitting, review your application for spelling and grammar mistakes.

Final Thoughts

Study tours are an excellent way for students to learn beyond textbooks. Visiting educational places, museums, and cultural sites helps students gain practical knowledge and new experiences.

Writing a proper study tour application ensures that you receive official permission from your school or college. By following the correct format and maintaining a polite tone, you can easily write an effective application.

You can also use the examples in this guide as templates and adjust them according to your school or college requirements.

item.title: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh - Complete Guide 2026
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Everything a Bangladeshi student needs to know: choosing a country, IELTS requirements, scholarships, the visa process, and what to expect when you arrive.
item.content:encoded:
Every year, tens of thousands of Bangladeshi students leave for universities in the UK, Australia, Canada, the United States, Germany, Malaysia, and beyond. Studying abroad opens doors to world-class education, international work experience, and often a pathway to residency in a new country. But the process — from choosing a university to landing at the airport with a student visa in hand — can feel overwhelming if you don't know where to start.

This guide walks you through every stage of the journey, step by step, with specific information relevant to students from Bangladesh.

Why Study Abroad from Bangladesh?

Bangladesh has made enormous strides in its domestic university sector, but studying at a recognized international institution still carries significant advantages for Bangladeshi students:

  • Global degree recognition — Degrees from UK, Australian, Canadian, and American universities are accepted by employers worldwide without question.
  • Post-study work rights — The UK's Graduate Route visa (2 years), Australia's Temporary Graduate visa (2–4 years), and Canada's Post-Graduation Work Permit (up to 3 years) let you gain international work experience after graduating.
  • Pathways to residency — Canada and Australia in particular have structured immigration systems where studying locally can significantly strengthen a permanent residency application.
  • Research and facilities — Access to research labs, libraries, and academic networks that are simply unavailable in Bangladesh for most fields.
  • Personal growth — Language fluency, cultural adaptability, and independence are qualities that employers across every industry increasingly value.

Step-by-Step: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh

1

Decide What You Want to Study and Why

Before choosing a country or university, be clear on your field, level (undergraduate or postgraduate), and career goal. Different countries have different strengths — engineering in Germany, business in the UK, healthcare in Australia, technology in Canada. Your choice of field should drive your choice of destination.

2

Check Your Academic Eligibility

Most undergraduate programs abroad require your SSC and HSC results. A GPA of 4.00+ in HSC (out of 5.00) is generally competitive. For postgraduate programs, your bachelor's degree transcript is the key document — a CGPA of 3.00+ (out of 4.00) from a recognized Bangladesh university is typically the minimum. Use our HSC GPA Calculator and CGPA Calculator to verify your scores.

3

Take IELTS (or an Accepted Alternative)

For English-medium programs in the UK, Australia, Canada, and USA, an English language test is mandatory. IELTS Academic is the most widely accepted. Aim for at least 6.5 overall for most universities. See the IELTS requirements section below for country-by-country details.

4

Research Universities and Programs

Use official university websites, QS World University Rankings, and the Times Higher Education rankings. Apply to a range of universities — 2–3 reach schools, 3–4 target schools, and 2 safe options. Pay attention to entry requirements, tuition fees, and scholarship availability for international students.

5

Apply for Scholarships Early

Scholarships have earlier deadlines than university applications — sometimes by 3–6 months. Research government scholarships (Chevening, Australia Awards, Commonwealth) and university merit scholarships simultaneously with your applications.

6

Submit University Applications

Prepare your Statement of Purpose (SOP), academic transcripts, recommendation letters (usually 2–3), CV, and proof of English proficiency. Deadlines vary — UK universities via UCAS typically close in January for September intake; Australian and Canadian universities often have rolling admissions.

7

Apply for Your Student Visa

Once you have a Conditional or Unconditional Offer and have accepted it, you can apply for a student visa. You will need proof of funds (typically covering 1 year of tuition + living costs), your offer letter, IELTS results, and passport photos. Apply at least 3 months before your course start date.

8

Prepare to Depart

Arrange student accommodation (university halls or private), open a student bank account in your destination country (many banks let you do this online before arriving), sort travel and health insurance, and attend any pre-departure orientation offered by your university or the Bangladesh embassy.

IELTS Score Requirements by Country

The IELTS Academic test is required for admission to most English-medium programs abroad. Here are the typical minimum requirements by destination country. Note that individual programs may require higher scores.

Country Undergraduate Minimum Postgraduate Minimum No Band Below
🇬🇧 United Kingdom 6.0 overall 6.5 overall 5.5
🇦🇺 Australia 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5 overall 6.0
🇨🇦 Canada 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5–7.0 overall 6.0
🇺🇸 United States 6.5 overall 7.0 overall 6.0
🇩🇪 Germany 6.0 (English programs) 6.5 (English programs) 5.5
🇲🇾 Malaysia 5.5–6.0 overall 6.0–6.5 overall 5.0
🇳🇿 New Zealand 6.0 overall 6.5 overall 5.5

💡 Tip

Use our free IELTS Band Score Calculator to estimate your overall band from your section scores. Aim to score at least 0.5 above the minimum requirement to give yourself a buffer.

Choosing the Right Country

United Kingdom

The UK remains one of the most popular destinations for Bangladeshi students. Undergraduate degrees take 3 years (saving one year vs Bangladesh or the US), and the Graduate Route visa allows 2 years of post-study work after graduation (3 years for PhD graduates). Tuition fees range from £10,000 to £38,000 per year. Living costs in London are significantly higher than other cities — consider universities in Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, or Sheffield for better value.

Australia

Australia offers a high quality of life and strong student work rights — you can work up to 48 hours per fortnight while studying. The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) allows 2–4 years of work rights after graduation, depending on the qualification and state where you study. Tuition fees range from AUD 20,000 to AUD 45,000 per year. Sydney and Melbourne are expensive; consider Brisbane, Adelaide, or Perth.

Canada

Canada has one of the clearest pathways from student to permanent resident. The Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) allows up to 3 years of work after completing a degree of 2+ years. Points earned from a Canadian degree and work experience can be used in the Express Entry immigration system. Tuition varies widely — CAD 15,000 to CAD 35,000 per year for international students.

Germany

Public universities in Germany charge little to no tuition fees for international students — you typically pay only a semester fee of €150–400. The catch is that most programs at the bachelor's level are taught in German. However, Germany has a rapidly growing number of English-taught master's programs, particularly in engineering, computer science, and business. Living costs are moderate at approximately €800–1,100 per month.

Malaysia

Malaysia is an increasingly popular and affordable alternative for Bangladeshi students. Tuition fees are significantly lower (MYR 15,000–60,000 per year), the cost of living is manageable, and many universities offer programs taught in English. It is also geographically and culturally closer to Bangladesh, making it easier for students who haven't studied or lived far from home before.

Cost of Studying Abroad from Bangladesh

Country Tuition (per year) Living Costs (per month) Work Rights
UK £10,000–£38,000 £800–£1,500 20 hrs/week term-time
Australia AUD 20,000–45,000 AUD 1,500–2,500 48 hrs/fortnight
Canada CAD 15,000–35,000 CAD 1,200–2,000 20 hrs/week off-campus
Germany €0–500 (public) €800–1,100 120 full days/year
Malaysia MYR 15,000–60,000 MYR 1,500–2,500 20 hrs/week (approved jobs)

ℹ️ Note

Exchange rates fluctuate significantly against the Bangladeshi Taka. Always budget with a 10–15% buffer and monitor rates using a reliable financial app before sending money abroad.

Scholarships for Bangladeshi Students

Funding your education abroad is the biggest challenge most Bangladeshi families face. The good news: there are dozens of scholarships specifically open to Bangladeshi students.

Government-Funded Scholarships

  • Chevening Scholarship (UK) — Fully funded by the UK government for outstanding future leaders. Covers tuition, living allowance, flights, and visa. For postgraduate study only. Deadline is typically November each year.
  • Australia Awards Scholarship — Fully funded by the Australian government for students from developing countries. Covers tuition, travel, Overseas Student Health Cover, and a living allowance. Very competitive — apply 12–18 months in advance.
  • Commonwealth Scholarship — For students from Commonwealth countries including Bangladesh. Covers full study costs for master's and PhD programs at UK universities.
  • DAAD Scholarship (Germany) — The German Academic Exchange Service offers numerous scholarships for Bangladeshi students for study and research in Germany. Many cover tuition, health insurance, and a monthly stipend of around €850–1,200.
  • Erasmus+ Scholarship (Europe) — Supports study or traineeships at European universities. Bangladesh students at eligible partner universities can apply.
  • China Government Scholarship (CSC) — Fully funded scholarships for undergraduate, master's, and PhD study at Chinese universities. No tuition fees, free accommodation, health insurance, and a monthly stipend.

University Merit Scholarships

Most universities in the UK, Australia, and Canada offer merit-based scholarships or fee reductions for high-achieving international students. These range from 10% to 100% of tuition. Check each university's international scholarships page — deadlines are usually the same as or shortly after the application deadline.

💡 Tip

Apply for scholarships and universities simultaneously. Many scholarship applications require a university offer letter, so begin both processes at the same time rather than waiting for admission before starting your scholarship search.

Documents You Will Need

  • Valid passport — At least 18 months validity beyond your course end date
  • SSC and HSC transcripts and certificates — Attested by the Bangladesh education board
  • Bachelor's degree transcript and provisional certificate (for postgraduate applicants)
  • IELTS Academic result — Original TRF (Test Report Form), usually valid for 2 years
  • Statement of Purpose (SOP) — 500–1,000 words explaining why you want to study this program
  • 2–3 Reference Letters — From academic supervisors or professors who know your work
  • CV/Resume — Academic and extracurricular achievements
  • Bank statement — Showing sufficient funds (usually 12 months of tuition + living costs)
  • Passport-size photographs — Requirements vary by country
  • Health insurance / OSHC — Required before visa issuance in Australia

Frequently Asked Questions

What IELTS score do I need to study abroad from Bangladesh?

Most programs in the UK, Australia, and Canada require 6.0–6.5 overall for undergraduate and 6.5–7.0 for postgraduate. No individual band should fall below 5.5 in most cases. Use our IELTS calculator to check your estimated score.

How much money do I need to show in my bank for a student visa?

Requirements vary by country. For a UK Student visa, you typically need to show funds covering 9 months of tuition + £1,334/month living costs (outside London) or £1,023/month (in London). For Australia, you need to show AUD 21,041 per year for living expenses, plus your full tuition. For Canada, you need CAD 10,000 per year above tuition. These figures are updated periodically — check the official embassy website before applying.

Can I study abroad from Bangladesh without IELTS?

Some universities accept TOEFL, PTE Academic, or Duolingo English Test as alternatives. Germany, Japan, and China offer programs in languages other than English. A few UK universities also waive IELTS if your previous education was conducted entirely in English — check individual institution policies.

Which country is easiest for Bangladeshi students to get a student visa?

Malaysia and Germany have relatively straightforward student visa processes for Bangladeshi nationals. The UK and Australia are more rigorous but manageable with proper documentation. Canada has become stricter in recent years; ensure your financial documents are clear and your study permit application is complete.

Can I work while studying abroad?

Yes, in most countries. The UK allows 20 hours/week during term time. Australia allows 48 hours per fortnight. Canada allows 20 hours/week off-campus. Germany allows 120 full working days per year. Always check the specific conditions of your visa — working beyond permitted hours can jeopardize your visa status.
